rv.q: The newest example of this trend, IT’S BEEN TEN YEARS SINCE EVERYBODY DIED, misses the mark on both scares and astute social commentary, but through no fault of its talented and refreshingly diverse cast.
Those who love their horror delivered with a bit of progressive, wildly queer energy should definitely find much to rejoice in here...

This seething agglomeration of distress is roused by a fortuitous thunderstorm, which not only provides appropriate auditory context (sound design Kiera Battles) but knocks out the camp’s electricity, so the remainder of the action is lit by lightning flashes (lighting design Lex Newman).
But Tirado-Ortiz's story... shows a playwright with promise and moxie.
But sadly, this play by Cesario Tirado-Ortiz, who “creates queer stories for queer folks,” was merely interesting but ultimately disappointing.
This show is a unique experience and you will be talking about it long after the actors take their bow.
It’s Been Ten Years Since Everyone Died blends together a horror story and a story about identity.

cn.t: Critics find this queer-themed horror play an intriguing but uneven exploration of final girl trauma, praising its unique premise and performances while noting the production feels rough and underdeveloped.
